concept: Solving trig equations in an interval
prompt:
**(a)** Solve $2\sin x=\sqrt3$ for $0\le x\le2\pi$. **[2]**

**(b)** Solve $\tan2x=1$ for $0\le x\le\pi$. **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $\sin x=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$: $x=\dfrac\pi3,\ \dfrac{2\pi}{3}$ **(A1)(A1)**

**(b)** $0\le2x\le2\pi$ and $\tan2x=1$: $2x=\dfrac\pi4,\ \dfrac{5\pi}{4}$ **(M1)**, so $x=\dfrac\pi8,\ \dfrac{5\pi}{8}$ **(A1)**

**Common mistake (b):** dividing too early and missing $\frac{5\pi}{8}$. Find all values of $2x$ in the doubled interval first.

$1-2\sin^{2}x=\sin x$ **(M1)** $\Rightarrow2\sin^{2}x+\sin x-1=0$ **(A1)**

$(2\sin x-1)(\sin x+1)=0$, so $\sin x=\tfrac12$ or $\sin x=-1$ **(A1)**

$x=\dfrac\pi6,\ \dfrac{5\pi}{6},\ \dfrac{3\pi}{2}$ **(A2)**
